The new oracle checks the two stated structural requirements as graph checks, and the 8 kHz audio rate is observed on audio.dat. (1) A Hilbert block (hilbert_fc) lies on a source -> File Sink path. (2) The SSB is made from the 8 kHz audio: a rate-increasing block lies on a source -> File Sink path; the id list holds every GNU Radio 3.10 block that can raise the rate. Authoring probes against the final task.json: the filter method (DSB + band-pass) fails the Hilbert checks. A graph that writes the 8 kHz audio to audio.dat but makes the SSB from a second copy of the tones generated at 48 kHz fails the rate-change path; it had passed before that check was added, and its cell combine|hilbert|mix|tone is a test cell. A new DSB mutant (Hilbert replaced by Float To Complex) is killed by the signal checks and the graph checks.

Own finding during calibration. With the planner's 1.9 kHz upper tone, a Repeat x6 (zero-order hold) + low-pass + Hilbert answer passed V5, although its droop leaves the 1.9 kHz tone 9 % low, against the stated 5 %. Shares 0.249 vs min 0.242; rms -3.4 %. The upper tone was moved to 2.4 kHz, where the droop is -14 %. Now share 0.230 < 0.2422 and 0.770 > 0.7578, so it fails V5 (probe against the final task.json). Every answer with both amplitudes within 5 % still passes. The remaining looseness of the share + rms bounds is review.notes limit (5).

Variants v1-v4 kept, plus new v5: an interpolating Low Pass Filter as the only rate changer, a Blackman Hilbert, and a Frequency Xlating FIR (taps [1], centre -10 kHz) as the up-shift. The other variants are: v1 Hilbert at 8 kHz + complex Rational Resampler + Rotator; v2 zero-stuffing + LPF + the classic I*cos - Q*sin phasing modulator; v3 Interpolating FIR + 129-tap Hilbert + Rotator; v4 PFB arbitrary resampler + 401-tap Kaiser Hilbert + Multiply Conjugate + Throttle + absolute paths. All 5 pass V5 and share the reference's v2 signature.

review.notes lists the known limits: (1) a Hilbert block on a side branch is not detected; (2) only hilbert_fc counts, because the instruction names GNU Radio's Hilbert block. Filter Delay with firdes.hilbert taps and FIR + Delay fail the graph check but pass every signal check (probe). Their v2 cells are other:filter_delay_fc -> test and ...|delay|... -> train. This is flagged for the team. (3) Hilbert length calibration: 65 taps at 48 kHz fail, 93 fail narrowly, 97 pass; at 8 kHz the default passes. (4) The rate-change check cannot read filter rate parameters: a 48 kHz tone copy whose path holds a Low Pass Filter passes. (5) Amplitude looseness. Disjointness names t01/t24, t16, t10 and the GRC-Agent scenario 21_type_conversion_and_conjugate.

rejected.reason: The plan's suggested variant 'Repeat + low-pass + Hilbert' is not a correct answer under the stated 5 % amplitude tolerance. A zero-order hold droops by sinc(f/8 kHz): -9.0 % at 1.9 kHz and -14.2 % at 2.4 kHz. It is not added as a variant, and the oracle now rejects it (authoring probe: V5 fails on both share checks).

Not added as a separate mutant: the near miss 'num_taps 65 at 48 kHz' (the block default) tests the same Hilbert-length requirement closer to the threshold (LSB share 7.2e-3 against 3.23e-4). A 9-tap Hilbert would only be a coarser copy of that mutant.
